quotes_en: Once Zhuang Zhou dreamt he was a butterfly, fluttering about, a butterfly to all purposes... He did not know whether he was Zhou who had dreamt he was a butterfly, or a butterfly dreaming he was Zhou. ("The Equality of Things")
Everyone knows the usefulness of the useful, but no one knows the usefulness of the useless. ("In the Human World")
works: 《庄子》（内篇七、外篇、杂篇；今本三十三篇，郭象注）
其中尤以内篇《逍遥游》《齐物论》《养生主》《人间世》《大宗师》最为核心
works_en: Zhuangzi (also rendered The Book of Master Zhuang; the Inner, Outer, and Miscellaneous Chapters—thirty-three in the received Guo Xiang recension)
of which the Inner Chapters—especially "Free and Easy Wandering," "The Equality of Things," "The Secret of Caring for Life," "In the Human World," and "The Great and Venerable Teacher"—are the core
zhuangzi.lineage: 上承老子的「道」与「无为」，下启魏晋玄学（与《老子》《周易》并称「三玄」）；融入汉传禅宗，并通过郭象注、林希逸等历代诠释绵延不绝；近世经理雅各、华兹生 (Burton Watson) 等译介西传，深受海德格尔等西方思想家关注。
zhuangzi.lineage_en: He inherited Laozi's "Dao" and "non-action" and gave rise to the Neo-Daoist "Mysterious Learning" of the Wei-Jin era (the Zhuangzi, Laozi, and Book of Changes were together called the "Three Mysteries"). His thought entered Chinese Chan Buddhism and was carried on through commentaries from Guo Xiang to Lin Xiyi; in modern times, through translations by James Legge, Burton Watson, and others, it reached the West and drew the keen interest of thinkers such as Heidegger.
zhuangzi.trivia: 妻子去世时，惠子前来吊唁，却见庄子「鼓盆而歌」——他解释：生死如四时更替，妻子已安息于天地巨室，自己再为之恸哭便是「不通乎命」；他与名家惠施亦敌亦友，「濠梁之辩」中那句「子非鱼，安知鱼之乐」的机锋问答，成为中国哲学史上最著名的辩论之一。
zhuangzi.trivia_en: When his wife died and his friend Huizi came to mourn, he found Zhuangzi "drumming on a tub and singing." He explained that life and death are like the turning of the four seasons—his wife now rested in the great chamber of heaven and earth, and to wail over it would be "not to understand fate." His sparring friendship with the logician Hui Shi produced the famous "Debate on the Bridge over the Hao," whose retort—"You are not a fish; how do you know the joy of fishes?"—remains one of the most celebrated exchanges in Chinese philosophy.

freud.bio: 1856–1939，奥地利神经科医生，精神分析学派的创立者，犹太人。在维也纳行医执教数十年，以对歇斯底里、梦与潜意识的研究开创了一门全新的学科。1938 年纳粹吞并奥地利后被迫流亡伦敦，次年因长年颌部癌症痛楚难当，在医生协助下注射吗啡辞世。
freud.bio_en: 1856–1939, an Austrian neurologist of Jewish descent and the founder of psychoanalysis. Practicing and teaching in Vienna for decades, his studies of hysteria, dreams, and the unconscious opened up an entirely new discipline. After the Nazi annexation of Austria in 1938 he was forced into exile in London, and the following year, worn down by years of jaw cancer, he died after a physician administered, at his request, a dose of morphine.
freud.ideas:
弗洛伊德最颠覆性的主张是：你以为是「你」在做主，其实不是。他把人的心灵比作一座漂在海上的冰山——你能看见的、能用语言说清的那部分意识，只是露出水面的一角；水面之下庞大的、看不见的部分，他叫「潜意识」（unconscious，即你完全意识不到、却一直在暗中左右你的念头与欲望）。那些被你认为太羞耻、太危险而「压抑」（repression，把不能接受的念头硬按下去、假装它不存在）下去的欲望，并不会消失，而是改头换面地从水底冒出来——变成莫名的焦虑、口误（说漏嘴）、忘事，或夜里的梦。
为说清这股暗流如何运作，他把人格拆成三股力量。「本我」（id）是与生俱来的原始冲动，像个只会喊「我现在就要」的婴儿，只认快乐、不管现实；「超我」（superego）是从小被父母和社会规训出来的良心与道德戒律，像个时时挑剔的内在法官，专说「你不许」；夹在中间的是「自我」（ego），是你清醒理性的那部分，像个疲于奔命的调解人，一边压住本我的冲动、一边应付超我的指责、一边还要顾及现实，尽量谈出一个三方都能勉强接受的方案。许多内心冲突，本质就是这三方在你看不见的地方拉锯。
为了不被这场拉锯压垮，心会自动启用各种「防御机制」（defense mechanism，潜意识里自欺的小把戏）：把不快的事情干脆「忘掉」、把自己的恶意说成是别人对你有恶意（投射）、或把怒火转移到更安全的对象身上（比如挨了老板骂、回家踢猫）。这些机制能暂时止痛，却也让人看不清真相。
他还提出两个影响深远的观点。其一是「俄狄浦斯情结」（Oedipus complex）：幼儿在三到五岁会朦胧地依恋异性的一方父母、把同性的一方当成竞争对手，这段早年的家庭三角关系，他认为深刻塑造了一个人成年后的性格与爱欲模式——也就是说，今天的你，很大程度是被童年悄悄写好的。其二是「强迫性重复」（repetition compulsion）：人会身不由己地一次次重演旧日的创伤，明明痛苦，却像中了魔似地反复掉进同一个坑（总是爱上同一类伤害自己的人，便是一例）。而他认为，通往这片水下世界最好的入口就是梦——梦是「通往潜意识的康庄大道」，那些被白天压住的欲望，会在睡梦里乔装打扮地演出来。
今天他的许多具体结论已被修正甚至推翻，但「潜意识」「压抑」「防御机制」「童年塑造成年」这些观念，早已渗进日常语言和整个现代心理治疗的底层——光是「人并不完全了解自己」这一洞见，就足以让他成为绕不开的起点。
freud.ideas_en:
Freud's most subversive claim is this: you think "you" are in charge, but you are not. He compared the mind to an iceberg floating in the sea—the conscious part you can see and put into words is only the tip above the waterline; the vast, hidden bulk beneath is what he called the "unconscious" (the thoughts and desires you are completely unaware of, yet which steer you all along). The wishes you find too shameful or dangerous and so "repress" (push down and pretend don't exist) do not vanish; they resurface in disguise—as unexplained anxiety, slips of the tongue, forgetting, or dreams in the night.
To explain how this undercurrent works, he split the personality into three forces. The "id" is your raw, inborn drives, like an infant who can only scream "I want it now," recognizing only pleasure and ignoring reality. The "superego" is the conscience and moral rules drilled into you by parents and society, like a nagging inner judge who only ever says "you mustn't." Caught between them is the "ego," your clear-headed, rational self, like an exhausted mediator—holding down the id's impulses, fending off the superego's reproaches, and minding reality all at once, trying to broker a deal all three can grudgingly accept. Much of our inner conflict is really these three tugging against one another out of sight.
To keep this tug-of-war from crushing us, the mind automatically deploys "defense mechanisms" (little tricks of self-deception in the unconscious): simply "forgetting" something unpleasant, recasting our own hostility as someone else's hostility toward us (projection), or redirecting anger onto a safer target (scolded by the boss, you go home and kick the cat). These tricks dull the pain for a while, but they also blind us to the truth.
He also advanced two far-reaching ideas. The first is the "Oedipus complex": between roughly ages three and five, a child dimly attaches to the opposite-sex parent and treats the same-sex parent as a rival, and this early family triangle, he believed, deeply shapes one's adult character and patterns of love and desire—meaning that who you are today was, in large part, quietly written in childhood. The second is the "repetition compulsion": people helplessly reenact old wounds over and over, falling back into the very same pit as if under a spell even though it hurts (always falling for the same kind of person who mistreats you is one example). And the best entrance to this underwater world, he thought, is the dream—the "royal road to the unconscious"—where the wishes suppressed by day put on costumes and act themselves out in sleep.
Today many of his specific conclusions have been revised or overturned, yet notions like the "unconscious," "repression," "defense mechanisms," and "childhood shapes the adult" have long since seeped into everyday language and into the foundations of all modern psychotherapy—the single insight that "we do not fully know ourselves" is enough to make him an unavoidable starting point.

assessments.text: 其影响远溢出诊室，重塑了文学、艺术、电影与日常语言——「潜意识」「压抑」「弗洛伊德式口误」早已成为现代人的常用词汇，奥登称他「已不只是一个人，而是一整套舆论氛围」。
在科学哲学上质疑精神分析「不可证伪」：任何结果都能被它自圆其说，因而不合乎可检验的科学标准；当代「可复制性」之争中，亦不乏对其理论实证基础的怀疑。平心而论，这些批评针对的是其方法的科学地位，而非否认其作为思想与文化现象的深远分量。

assessments_en.text: His influence spilled far beyond the consulting room, reshaping literature, art, film, and everyday language—"the unconscious," "repression," and the "Freudian slip" long ago became common modern vocabulary; W. H. Auden wrote that he was "no more a person now but a whole climate of opinion."

In the philosophy of science, Popper charged that psychoanalysis is "unfalsifiable"—able to explain any outcome after the fact and therefore failing the test of genuine scientific theory; the contemporary "replication" debates have likewise voiced doubts about its empirical footing. In fairness, these criticisms target the scientific standing of his method, not the profound weight of his thought as an intellectual and cultural phenomenon.

quotes: 梦是通往潜意识的康庄大道。（《梦的解析》）
未被言说的情绪不会消亡，它们只是被活埋，日后会以更丑陋的方式重现。（大意）
quotes_en: The interpretation of dreams is the royal road to the unconscious. (The Interpretation of Dreams)
Unexpressed emotions will never die; they are buried alive and will come forth later in uglier ways. (paraphrased)
works_en: Three Essays on the Theory of Sexuality
freud.lineage: 受布罗伊尔的「谈话疗法」与夏柯的催眠研究启发；门下的阿德勒、荣格先后与他决裂，各自开宗立派；其思想经女儿安娜·弗洛伊德、克莱因、拉康等人分流演变，深刻塑造了二十世纪的心理治疗、人文与社会思想。
freud.lineage_en: He was inspired by Josef Breuer's "talking cure" and Charcot's work on hypnosis; his disciples Adler and Jung each broke with him to found their own schools. His thought branched and evolved through Anna Freud, Melanie Klein, Jacques Lacan, and others, profoundly shaping twentieth-century psychotherapy and the humanities and social sciences.
freud.trivia: 他是个重度雪茄客，一生戒不掉，最终也死于与之相关的颌癌；他酷爱收藏古希腊罗马与埃及文物，案头摆满小雕像，自比为发掘心灵地层的「考古学家」。
freud.trivia_en: A heavy cigar smoker who could never quit, he ultimately died of the jaw cancer linked to the habit. He was an avid collector of Greek, Roman, and Egyptian antiquities, his desk crowded with small statues, and he likened himself to an "archaeologist" excavating the buried strata of the mind.

adler.bio: 1870–1937，奥地利医生、心理治疗师，「个体心理学」(individual psychology) 的创立者。早年是弗洛伊德圈子的核心成员，1911 年因学说分歧与之决裂。一战中任军医，目睹战争之恶，此后更强调人的社会性与平等。晚年赴美讲学，1937 年在苏格兰巡讲途中猝逝。
adler.bio_en: 1870–1937, an Austrian physician and psychotherapist, founder of "individual psychology." Once a central member of Freud's circle, he broke with him in 1911 over differences of doctrine. Serving as an army doctor in the First World War, he witnessed the cruelty of war and thereafter stressed all the more the social nature and equality of human beings. In his later years he lectured in America, and in 1937 he died suddenly while on a speaking tour in Scotland.
adler.ideas:
阿德勒也曾是弗洛伊德圈子的核心成员，最终却另立门户，原因正在于他对「人是什么」给出了截然相反的答案。他的起点是一个谁都体会过的感受——「自卑感」（人觉得自己不够好、比别人差的那种感觉）。在他看来这并非毛病，而是普遍且健康的动力：每个人都从小时候那种又小又无力的处境出发，于是终其一生都在「追求优越」（striving for superiority，努力让自己变得更强、更有价值），靠奋斗去「补偿」（compensation，用别处的长处来弥补自己的短处）那份不足。许多了不起的成就，背后正是这股想超越自卑的劲。但若这份自卑被无力感压垮、僵死成「我就是不行」的固执信念，就变成有害的「自卑情结」（inferiority complex）。
他认为健康人生的关键，在于「社会兴趣」（德文 Gemeinschaftsgefühl，可译为「共同体感觉」）——一种把自己看作群体一员、真心关切他人福祉、愿与人合作的情怀。心理是否健康，他几乎用这一条来衡量：一个人越是只盯着自己的优越、越孤立，就越痛苦；越能在「我能为他人、为共同体做点什么」里找到位置，就越踏实幸福。
他还格外强调「创造性自我」：人不是被基因、环境或往事捏成的泥人，而是主动的解释者——同样的经历，你怎么理解它、赋予它什么意义，取决于你自己，并由此一点点塑造出独属于你的「生活风格」（lifestyle，一个人面对世界的整套惯常打法）。
他思想中最锋利、也最反弗洛伊德的一点，是「目的论」（teleology，用「为了什么目的」而非「由于什么原因」来解释行为）。弗洛伊德说你今天的样子，是被童年的因「推」出来的；阿德勒反过来说：人是被自己设定的未来「目标」所「牵引」的。换句话说，决定你的不是过去发生了什么，而是你为了某个目的，赋予了过去什么意义。一个人之所以走不出旧伤，未必是创伤本身使然，而可能是他（往往不自觉地）正用这道伤，来达成「不必去冒险改变」的当下目的。这一「重要的不是被给予了什么，而是如何运用它」的立场，正是反对一切「你已被注定」之决定论的鲜明旗帜。
正因为把改变的主动权交还给个人，阿德勒的思想格外贴近现代生活。近年风靡的畅销书《被讨厌的勇气》便是对他学说的通俗演绎——它告诉读者：你随时可以重新选择如何解释自己的人生，而这，正是阿德勒一个世纪前就想交到每个人手里的自由。
adler.ideas_en:
Adler too was once a core member of Freud's circle, yet in the end he broke away to found his own school—precisely because he gave the opposite answer to the question of what a human being is. His starting point is a feeling everyone has known: "inferiority" (the sense of not being good enough, of falling short of others). In his view this is no defect but a universal and healthy engine: each of us starts from the small, helpless condition of childhood, and so spends a whole life "striving for superiority" (working to become stronger and more worthy), using "compensation" (making up for a weakness with strength somewhere else) to offset that shortfall. Behind many great achievements is exactly this drive to outgrow one's own inferiority. But if that inferiority is crushed by helplessness and hardens into the rigid conviction "I just can't," it becomes the harmful "inferiority complex."
The key to a healthy life, he held, is "social interest" (in German, Gemeinschaftsgefühl, "community feeling")—a disposition to see oneself as one member of a group, to genuinely care about others' welfare, and to want to cooperate. He measured psychological health almost entirely by this: the more a person fixates only on his own superiority and isolates himself, the more he suffers; the more he can find a place in "what can I do for others, for the community," the more grounded and happy he is.
He laid special stress on the "creative self": a person is not a lump of clay molded by genes, environment, or the past, but an active interpreter—the same experience can mean different things depending on how you understand it, and through that you gradually shape a "lifestyle" all your own (your whole habitual way of meeting the world).
The sharpest and most anti-Freudian point in his thought is "teleology" (explaining behavior by "for what purpose" rather than "because of what cause"). Freud said who you are today was "pushed" out of you by causes in childhood; Adler reversed it: a person is "pulled" by the future goals he sets himself. In other words, what decides you is not what happened in the past but what meaning you, for some present purpose, assign to the past. Someone unable to move past an old wound may not be held there by the trauma itself, but may be (usually unwittingly) using that wound to serve a present aim—"not having to risk changing." This stance—"what matters is not what you were given, but how you use it"—is a clear banner against every determinism that says "you are already fated."
Because it hands the power to change back to the individual, Adler's thought feels strikingly close to modern life. The recent bestseller The Courage to Be Disliked is a popular retelling of his ideas—it tells readers that you can choose, at any moment, to reinterpret your own life; and this is exactly the freedom Adler wanted to place in everyone's hands a century ago.

assessments.text: 其重认知、重目标、重当下选择的取向，被视为认知行为疗法 (CBT) 与人本主义、家庭治疗的重要先声；许多今日耳熟能详的观念（如「自卑情结」）皆出自他手。
二人以对话体著作《被讨厌的勇气》通俗演绎阿德勒思想，全球热销，使这位长期被弗洛伊德、荣格光芒所掩的思想家在二十一世纪重获大量读者。

assessments_en.text: His emphasis on cognition, on goals, and on present choice is seen as an important forerunner of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and of humanistic and family therapy; many ideas now taken for granted (such as the "inferiority complex") came from him.

Their dialogue-form book The Courage to Be Disliked popularized Adler's thought and became a global bestseller, winning a vast new readership in the twenty-first century for a thinker long overshadowed by Freud and Jung.

quotes: 重要的不是一个人天生拥有什么，而是他如何运用所拥有的。（大意）
决定我们的，不是过去的经历本身，而是我们赋予它的意义。（大意，阿德勒心理学要旨）
quotes_en: What matters is not what one is born with, but the use one makes of it. (paraphrased)
We are determined not by our experiences themselves, but by the meaning we give them. (paraphrased; a core tenet of Adlerian psychology)
works: 《自卑与超越》（直译《生活对你应有的意义》）
works_en: What Life Could Mean to You
The Practice and Theory of Individual Psychology
adler.lineage: 出于弗洛伊德圈子又与之决裂，与荣格并为最早的两位「叛徒」；其思想经霍妮、弗洛姆等新弗洛伊德派与人本主义传承，并通过《被讨厌的勇气》在东亚广泛流行；与同样强调意义与态度选择的弗兰克尔（维也纳第三学派）遥相呼应。
adler.lineage_en: Emerging from Freud's circle and then breaking with it, he was, alongside Jung, one of the first two "defectors." His ideas were carried on by neo-Freudians and humanists such as Karen Horney and Erich Fromm, and spread widely across East Asia through The Courage to Be Disliked; they resonate with Frankl's "Third Viennese School," which likewise stresses meaning and the choice of one's attitude.
adler.trivia: 他幼时体弱多病，曾患佝偻病、险些死于肺炎，又两度被车撞——亲历的虚弱与「自卑」据信正是其学说的种子；他主张心理学应走出诊室、面向大众，常以平实语言公开演讲，是最早推动儿童教育辅导与社区心理工作的先驱之一。
adler.trivia_en: Sickly as a child—he suffered from rickets, nearly died of pneumonia, and was twice run over by carriages—his firsthand experience of frailty and "inferiority" is thought to be the very seed of his theory. He believed psychology should leave the consulting room for the wider public, lectured openly in plain language, and was among the first to pioneer child guidance and community mental-health work.

jung.bio: 1875–1961，瑞士精神病学家，分析心理学 (analytical psychology) 的创立者。曾是弗洛伊德最器重的「太子」与指定继承人，1913 年因学说分歧（尤其对「力比多」是否纯属性欲）与之决裂，此后经历一段深刻的内在危机与自我探索。一生著述宏富，晚年隐居苏黎世湖畔的波林根塔楼。
jung.bio_en: 1875–1961, a Swiss psychiatrist and the founder of analytical psychology. Once Freud's most prized "crown prince" and designated heir, he broke with him in 1913 over differences of doctrine (above all whether "libido" is purely sexual), and afterward passed through a profound inner crisis and self-exploration. Prolific throughout his life, in his later years he lived in seclusion at his stone tower in Bollingen on the shore of Lake Zürich.
jung.ideas:
荣格曾是弗洛伊德最看重的接班人，后来却分道扬镳。他接受老师「潜意识」（意识不到、却暗中影响你的那部分心灵）的洞见，但走得更远。弗洛伊德的潜意识装的是「你个人」被压抑的私货；荣格说，在那层「个体潜意识」之下，还有一层全人类共享的「集体潜意识」（collective unconscious）——它不是你这辈子攒下来的，而是像本能一样，由千万年来无数祖先的共同经验沉淀、遗传给每一个人的心理底座。
这片共同的深层里住着「原型」（archetype，人类经验反复出现的、放之四海皆准的基本模板或角色）。它们不是具体的画面，而像一套预装好的「插槽」，会在各民族的神话、宗教、童话里反复显形：慈爱又吞噬的「母亲」、智慧的「老者」、英雄、骗子……为什么全世界的故事都有这些似曾相识的角色？荣格的答案是：因为它们本就刻在我们共同的心底。
在众多原型里，他最看重几个。「阴影」（shadow）是你不肯承认、嫌弃并藏起来的那部分自己——你的自私、嫉妒、攻击性；越是假装没有，它越会在背后捣乱（你最讨厌别人身上的某个毛病，往往正是你的阴影）。「人格面具」（persona）是你戴给世界看的那张社会面孔，像演员的面具；好用，但若把面具当成真自己，人就空掉了。「阿尼玛/阿尼姆斯」（anima/animus）则是男人心里那个女性的一面、女人心里那个男性的一面——人要变得完整，就得认领被自己压住的异性特质。
把这些碎片一一找回、整合成一个完整的自己，他叫「个体化」（individuation）——这是他眼中人一生最重要的功课：不是变得更「正常」、更合群，而是成为那个独一无二、表里如一的你。他还顺手开创了人格分类：把人分为能量向内、靠独处充电的「内倾」和能量向外、靠人群充电的「外倾」（今天大众挂在嘴边的「内向/外向」即源于此），并由此发展出后来 MBTI 性格测验的雏形。晚年他更提出一个大胆概念「共时性」（synchronicity）：有些「有意义的巧合」（比如刚想起某人电话就响了）之间未必有因果关系，却仿佛被某种意义牵在一起。
和弗洛伊德盯着病理与压抑不同，荣格的眼光朝向成长、意义与精神的完整。他把神话、炼金术、东方哲学都纳进心理学，至今深刻影响着心理治疗、文学分析乃至流行文化里无处不在的「英雄之旅」叙事。
jung.ideas_en:
Jung was once Freud's most favored heir, and then they parted ways. He accepted his teacher's insight into the "unconscious" (the part of the mind you're unaware of that influences you in secret), but he pushed further. Freud's unconscious held "your" personal, repressed baggage; Jung said that beneath that "personal unconscious" lies a deeper layer shared by all humankind—the "collective unconscious." It is not something you accumulated in this lifetime but, like instinct, a psychic bedrock laid down over millions of years from the shared experience of countless ancestors and inherited by everyone.
Dwelling in this common depth are the "archetypes" (the recurring, universal templates or roles of human experience). They are not specific pictures but something like pre-installed "slots" that surface again and again in the myths, religions, and fairy tales of every culture: the loving yet devouring "Mother," the wise "Old Man," the hero, the trickster. Why do stories the world over feature these strangely familiar figures? Jung's answer: because they are etched into the floor of our shared mind.
Among the many archetypes he prized a few above all. The "shadow" is the part of yourself you refuse to admit, dislike, and hide away—your selfishness, envy, aggression; the harder you pretend it isn't there, the more it sabotages you from behind (the trait you most loathe in others is often your own shadow). The "persona" is the social face you put on for the world, like an actor's mask; useful, but mistake the mask for the real you and the self goes hollow. The "anima/animus" is the feminine side within a man and the masculine side within a woman—to become whole, one must reclaim the opposite-sex qualities one has suppressed.
Gathering up these fragments and integrating them into a complete self is what he called "individuation"—in his eyes the most important task of a life: not becoming more "normal" or more agreeable, but becoming the one unique, undivided you. He also founded personality typing along the way: dividing people into the "introvert," whose energy turns inward and who recharges in solitude, and the "extravert," whose energy turns outward and who recharges among people (today's casual talk of "introvert/extrovert" comes straight from here), out of which grew the seed of the later MBTI test. In old age he proposed the bold notion of "synchronicity": certain "meaningful coincidences" (you think of someone and the phone rings) need have no cause-and-effect link, yet seem bound together by some thread of meaning.
Unlike Freud, fixed on pathology and repression, Jung looked toward growth, meaning, and spiritual wholeness. He folded myth, alchemy, and Eastern philosophy into psychology, and to this day he shapes psychotherapy, literary analysis, and the ever-present "hero's journey" narrative of popular culture.

assessments.text: 他对内倾/外倾与心理功能的区分，经迈尔斯与布里格斯母女发展为风靡全球的 MBTI 人格测验——尽管 MBTI 本身的科学效度屡受心理计量学界质疑，这一影响的广度却毋庸置疑。
主流实证心理学常批评其「原型」「集体潜意识」「共时性」等概念失之玄奥、难以操作化检验，更近神话学、宗教学而非自然科学；但他对叙事、象征与意义的洞察，在人文、宗教比较与深度心理治疗领域始终影响深远。

assessments_en.text: His distinction of introversion/extraversion and the psychological functions was developed by Katharine Briggs and Isabel Myers into the globally popular MBTI personality inventory—and while the scientific validity of the MBTI itself is repeatedly questioned by psychometricians, the breadth of this influence is beyond doubt.

Mainstream empirical psychology often faults concepts such as "archetypes," the "collective unconscious," and "synchronicity" as obscure and resistant to operationalized testing—closer to mythology and religious studies than to natural science; yet his insight into narrative, symbol, and meaning remains deeply influential in the humanities, comparative religion, and depth psychotherapy.

quotes: 除非你把潜意识变为意识，否则它将主宰你的人生，而你会称之为命运。（语见《艾翁》及书信）
凡使我们对他人感到恼怒的一切，都能引领我们认识自己。（大意）
quotes_en: Until you make the unconscious conscious, it will direct your life and you will call it fate. (from Aion and his letters)
Everything that irritates us about others can lead us to an understanding of ourselves. (paraphrased)
works: 《回忆·梦·思考》（自传，与阿尼拉·雅菲合著）
works_en: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious
Memories, Dreams, Reflections (autobiography, with Aniela Jaffé)
jung.lineage: 出于弗洛伊德门下又与之决裂，自立分析心理学；上承尼采、歌德、炼金术与诺斯替传统，并广采东方思想（《易经》《西藏度亡经》《太乙金华宗旨》）；影响及于神话学家坎贝尔、人格类型学、深度心理学、新纪元运动与比较宗教学。
jung.lineage_en: Coming out of Freud's school and then breaking with it, he founded analytical psychology on his own; he drew on Nietzsche, Goethe, alchemy, and the Gnostic tradition, and ranged widely over Eastern thought (the I Ching, the Tibetan Book of the Dead, The Secret of the Golden Flower). His influence reached the mythologist Joseph Campbell, personality typology, depth psychology, the New Age movement, and comparative religion.
jung.trivia: 与弗洛伊德决裂后，他经历一段濒临精神崩溃的「与无意识对峙」时期，把其间的幻象与对话绘记于神秘的《红书》——该书直到 2009 年才公开出版；他在波林根亲手垒石造塔，作为退隐与自省之所，称之为「石头里的告白」。
jung.trivia_en: After his break with Freud he passed through a near-breakdown, a "confrontation with the unconscious," recording its visions and dialogues in the mysterious Red Book—which was not published until 2009. At Bollingen he built a stone tower with his own hands as a place of retreat and reflection, calling it a "confession in stone."

kongzi.bio: 前551–前479，名丘，字仲尼，春秋末期鲁国陬邑人，儒家学派的创立者。出身没落贵族，幼年丧父，自学成才；中年曾短暂出仕鲁国，后率弟子周游列国十余年，欲以其道说服诸侯而终不得用。晚年归鲁，整理典籍、聚徒讲学，相传弟子三千、贤者七十二。后世尊为「至圣先师」。
kongzi.bio_en: 551–479 BC, named Qiu and styled Zhongni, a native of Zou in the state of Lu at the close of the Spring and Autumn period, and the founder of the Confucian tradition. Born into a declining aristocratic family and fatherless in childhood, he was largely self-taught. In middle age he briefly held office in Lu, then traveled among the states with his disciples for more than a decade, seeking in vain to persuade rulers to adopt his Way. In his later years he returned to Lu to edit the classics and teach; tradition holds that he had three thousand disciples, seventy-two of them accomplished. Later ages honored him as the "Supreme Sage and Foremost Teacher."
kongzi.ideas: 以「仁」为思想核心——「仁者爱人」，推己及人；以「礼」为社会秩序的规范，主张「克己复礼」；重「孝」为德行之本，倡「君子」作为德才兼备的理想人格；提出「正名」——名实相符，各安其分，社会方得其治；持「中庸」之道，不偏不倚，过犹不及；论政则主张「为政以德」，以身作则胜于严刑峻法。
kongzi.ideas_en: At the core of his thought is ren (benevolence)—"the benevolent person loves others," extending from oneself to others; li (ritual propriety) is the norm of social order, and he urged one to "subdue the self and return to ritual." He held filial piety (xiao) to be the root of virtue and upheld the junzi (the exemplary person) as the ideal of one accomplished in both virtue and ability. He proposed the "rectification of names"—that names accord with realities and each keep to its station, so that society may be well governed. He kept to the way of the mean (zhongyong), without bias or excess, holding that "going too far is as bad as falling short." In governance he argued for ruling by virtue, holding that leading by personal example surpasses harsh laws and punishments.

assessments.text: 其学说自汉代「独尊儒术」后成为中国两千年的官方意识形态与科举取士的根本经典，并远播朝鲜、日本、越南，深刻塑造了整个东亚的伦理、教育与政治传统，被视为中华文明最重要的精神奠基者。
二十世纪初的新文化运动高举「打倒孔家店」之旗，激烈批判以「礼教」为名的等级、宗法与对个人（尤其女性）的束缚，认为它阻碍了现代化与个性解放——这场对儒家纲常的批判，至今仍是评价孔子时无法回避的一面。

assessments_en.text: After the Han dynasty's "exclusive veneration of Confucianism," his teaching became China's official ideology for two thousand years and the foundational canon of the imperial examinations; spreading to Korea, Japan, and Vietnam, it profoundly shaped the ethics, education, and politics of all East Asia, and he is regarded as the most important spiritual founder of Chinese civilization.

In the early twentieth century the New Culture Movement raised the banner "Down with the House of Confucius," fiercely criticizing the hierarchy, clan order, and constraints on the individual (especially women) imposed in the name of "ritual teaching," which it held to obstruct modernization and the liberation of the person—a critique of the Confucian moral order that remains an inescapable side of any appraisal of Confucius.

quotes: 父母之年，不可不知也。一则以喜，一则以惧。（《论语·里仁》）
事父母几谏，见志不从，又敬不违，劳而不怨。（《论语·里仁》)
quotes_en: The years of one's parents must not be forgotten: on the one hand a source of joy, on the other of dread. (Analects, "Li Ren")
In serving your parents, remonstrate gently; if you see they are not inclined to heed you, remain respectful and do not disobey, and toil for them without complaint. (Analects, "Li Ren")
works: 《论语》（其言行由弟子及再传弟子辑录而成，非孔子自著）
相传曾删订《诗》《书》，订《礼》《乐》，作《春秋》，序《易传》（「六经」，传统说法）
works_en: The Analects (compiled by his disciples and their disciples from his words and deeds, not written by Confucius himself)

tradition credits him with editing the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents, ordering the Rites and Music, composing the Spring and Autumn Annals, and arranging the Commentaries on the Book of Changes (the "Six Classics," by traditional account)
kongzi.lineage: 上承周公之礼乐文明，自谓「述而不作，信而好古」；下经曾子、子思传至孟子（道性善、行仁政）与荀子（言性恶、隆礼重法），分立两脉；汉代立为官学，宋代经周敦颐、二程、朱熹发展为理学（新儒家），明代有王阳明心学；近世又有港台新儒家（牟宗三、唐君毅等）回应西学。
kongzi.lineage_en: He inherited the ritual-and-music civilization of the Duke of Zhou, saying of himself, "I transmit but do not create; I am faithful to and love the ancients." His Way passed through Zengzi and Zisi to Mencius (who taught the goodness of human nature and benevolent government) and Xunzi (who held that nature is bad and exalted ritual and law), forming two branches. Established as state learning in the Han, it was developed in the Song by Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, and Zhu Xi into Neo-Confucianism (Lixue), and in the Ming by Wang Yangming's "learning of the mind"; in modern times the New Confucians of Hong Kong and Taiwan (Mou Zongsan, Tang Junyi, and others) responded to Western thought.
kongzi.trivia: 他周游列国时曾在陈、蔡之间绝粮，随从弟子困病，子路愠见而问「君子亦有穷乎」，孔子答「君子固穷，小人穷斯滥矣」——身处困顿仍守其节；他自述生平「十有五而志于学，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳顺，七十而从心所欲，不逾矩」，成为后世形容人生阶段的经典话语。
kongzi.trivia_en: While traveling among the states he ran out of provisions between Chen and Cai; his followers fell ill and weak, and Zilu, vexed, asked, "Does even the exemplary person fall into such straits?" Confucius answered, "The exemplary person holds firm in adversity; the petty man, in adversity, gives way to excess"—keeping his integrity even in hardship. He described his own life thus: "At fifteen I set my heart on learning; at thirty I stood firm; at forty I had no doubts; at fifty I knew the will of Heaven; at sixty my ear was attuned; at seventy I could follow what my heart desired without overstepping the bounds"—words that became a classic way of marking the stages of a life.

socrates.bio: 约公元前470–前399年，古希腊雅典哲学家，西方哲学的奠基人物之一。他本人未留下任何著作，思想主要通过弟子柏拉图的对话录与色诺芬的记述流传。出身平民，曾以石匠为业，参加过伯罗奔尼撒战争；晚年以『腐蚀青年、不敬城邦诸神』之罪受审，被判饮鸩而死。
socrates.bio_en: c. 470–399 BC, an Athenian philosopher and one of the founders of Western philosophy. He left no writings of his own; his thought survives mainly through the dialogues of his pupil Plato and the memoirs of Xenophon. Born a commoner and reportedly a stonemason by trade, he served in the Peloponnesian War; late in life he was tried for 'corrupting the youth and impiety toward the city's gods' and sentenced to die by drinking hemlock.
socrates.ideas: 以『诘问法』(产婆术／反诘法)著称——通过连续追问揭示对话者概念的含混与自相矛盾，引人自省。主张『自知无知』(我只知道我一无所知)、『德性即知识』(无人有意作恶，作恶源于无知)、『未经省察的人生不值得过』。他把哲学的重心从对自然的思辨转向对人、伦理与如何生活的追问。
socrates.ideas_en: He is famous for the 'Socratic method' (elenchus, or 'midwifery'): a chain of questions that exposes the vagueness and self-contradiction in an interlocutor's concepts and prompts self-examination. He held that one should 'know that one knows nothing,' that 'virtue is knowledge' (no one does wrong willingly; wrongdoing springs from ignorance), and that 'the unexamined life is not worth living.' He turned the focus of philosophy from speculation about nature toward questions of the human being, ethics, and how to live.

assessments.text: 在《申辩篇》《斐多篇》等对话中将其塑造为为真理与德性殉道的典范，使苏格拉底成为后世哲学家的人格原型。
罗马的西塞罗有一著名评语，大意是『苏格拉底把哲学从天上带到了人间』——即从对天体自然的玄思，转向城邦与日常生活中的伦理问题。

assessments_en.text: In dialogues such as the Apology and the Phaedo, Plato cast him as a model martyr for truth and virtue, making Socrates the archetypal persona of the philosopher for later ages.

The Roman Cicero famously remarked, in paraphrase, that 'Socrates called philosophy down from the heavens'—turning it from speculation about the cosmos toward the ethical questions of the city and of everyday life.

quotes: 我只知道一件事，就是我一无所知。(传统归于苏格拉底的名言，大意)
未经省察的人生不值得过。(柏拉图《申辩篇》38a)
无人明知善而故意作恶；作恶皆出于无知。(柏拉图对话的主旨，大意)
quotes_en: I know one thing: that I know nothing. (a maxim traditionally attributed to Socrates, paraphrased)
The unexamined life is not worth living. (Plato, Apology 38a)
No one knowingly does evil; wrongdoing comes from ignorance. (the gist of Plato's dialogues, paraphrased)
works: 其思想见于柏拉图的对话录(《申辩篇》《克力同篇》《斐多篇》《会饮篇》等)
阿里斯托芬喜剧《云》(同时代的讽刺刻画)
works_en: His thought appears in Plato's dialogues (Apology, Crito, Phaedo, Symposium, and others)
Aristophanes' comedy The Clouds (a satirical portrait by a contemporary)
socrates.lineage: 上承前苏格拉底自然哲学并使之转向；下启弟子柏拉图及其学园，再经亚里士多德影响整个西方哲学传统；犬儒学派、斯多亚学派、怀疑论等也都把自己的源头追溯到他。
socrates.lineage_en: He inherited and redirected pre-Socratic natural philosophy; he gave rise to his pupil Plato and the Academy, and through Aristotle shaped the whole Western tradition; the Cynics, Stoics, and Skeptics all traced their lineage back to him as well.
socrates.trivia: 据传他常陷入出神的沉思，可在原地一连站立思索许久；他又自称有一个『daimonion』(内在的神异声音)，只在他将要做错事时出声制止。受审定罪后，朋友已为他安排好逃亡，他却拒绝，从容饮鸩而死，成为哲学史上著名的一幕。
socrates.trivia_en: He is said to have fallen into trances of thought, once standing rooted in one spot in contemplation for a long stretch; he also claimed an inner 'daimonion'—a divine sign—that spoke up only to stop him from doing wrong. After his conviction his friends arranged an escape, but he refused it and calmly drank the hemlock, in one of the most famous scenes in the history of philosophy.

turing.bio: 1912–1954，英国数学家、逻辑学家，理论计算机科学与人工智能的奠基人。1936 年提出抽象计算模型『图灵机』。二战期间在布莱切利园主导破译德军 Enigma 密码，对盟军胜利贡献卓著。战后从事早期计算机设计与生物形态发生研究。1952 年因同性恋(当时英国为刑事罪)被定罪并接受激素处置；1954 年去世，普遍认为系氰化物中毒。2013 年获英国王室追授赦免。
turing.bio_en: 1912–1954, a British mathematician and logician, founder of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence. In 1936 he set out the abstract model of computation now called the 'Turing machine.' During the Second World War he led the breaking of Germany's Enigma cipher at Bletchley Park, a decisive contribution to the Allied victory. After the war he worked on early computer design and on biological morphogenesis. In 1952 he was convicted of homosexuality (then a crime in Britain) and made to undergo hormone treatment; he died in 1954, widely held to be from cyanide poisoning. He received a posthumous royal pardon in 2013.
turing.ideas: 『图灵机』奠定可计算性理论，划定了算法可解的边界(并证明停机问题不可判定)；『通用图灵机』是现代存储程序计算机的理论原型。1950 年论文《计算机器与智能》提出『模仿游戏』(图灵测试)，把『机器能否思考』转译为可操作的行为判定，开人工智能之先河。晚年以反应—扩散方程解释生物图案的自发形成(『图灵斑图』)。
turing.ideas_en: The 'Turing machine' grounded the theory of computability, fixing the limits of what algorithms can solve (and proving the halting problem undecidable); the 'universal Turing machine' is the theoretical prototype of the modern stored-program computer. His 1950 paper 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' proposed the 'imitation game' (the Turing test), recasting 'can machines think?' as an operational, behavioral test and inaugurating artificial intelligence. Late in life he used reaction–diffusion equations to explain the spontaneous formation of biological patterns ('Turing patterns').

assessments.text: 计算机领域的最高荣誉以其命名为『图灵奖』(ACM Turing Award，常被称作计算机界的诺贝尔奖)；他本人被广泛尊为『计算机科学之父』与『人工智能之父』之一。
史界普遍认为布莱切利园对 Enigma 的破译显著缩短了战争、挽救了大量生命；他战后因性取向遭受的迫害，也成为后世反思的标志性案例。

assessments_en.text: The field's highest honor is named for him—the ACM Turing Award, often called the Nobel Prize of computing; he is widely revered as a father of computer science and of artificial intelligence.

Historians broadly hold that the Bletchley Park break of Enigma materially shortened the war and saved many lives; the persecution he suffered after it for his sexuality has become a landmark case for later reflection.

quotes: 我提议考虑这样一个问题：『机器能思考吗？』(《计算机器与智能》开篇，大意)
我们只能看到前方很短的距离，但已足见有大量工作亟待完成。(同文结尾，大意)
quotes_en: I propose to consider the question, 'Can machines think?' (opening of 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence,' paraphrased)
We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done. (closing of the same paper, paraphrased)
works: 《论可计算数及其在判定问题上的应用》(1936，提出图灵机)
《计算机器与智能》(1950，提出图灵测试)
works_en: 'On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem' (1936, introducing the Turing machine)
'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' (1950, introducing the Turing test)
turing.lineage: 上承希尔伯特的判定问题、哥德尔的不完备性与丘奇的 λ 演算(图灵与丘奇各自独立得到等价结论，史称『丘奇—图灵论题』)；下启冯·诺依曼体系结构、整个计算机科学与人工智能领域。
turing.lineage_en: He built on Hilbert's Entscheidungsproblem, Gödel's incompleteness, and Church's lambda calculus (Turing and Church reached equivalent results independently, in what is called the Church–Turing thesis); he gave rise to the von Neumann architecture and to the whole of computer science and artificial intelligence.
turing.trivia: 他是一名出色的长跑运动员，水平接近当时的奥运选拔标准；二战期间他担心德军入侵，把积蓄换成银条埋藏起来，战后却因记不清确切位置而始终没能寻回。床边一只被咬过、据信浸过氰化物的苹果，成为关于他死亡的著名意象(确切死因至今仍有争议)。
turing.trivia_en: He was a superb long-distance runner, close to Olympic-trial standard; fearing a German invasion during the war, he converted his savings into silver bars and buried them, but afterward could never recall the exact spot and never recovered them. A half-eaten apple by his bed, believed to have been laced with cyanide, became the famous image of his death (the precise cause is still debated).

wolf.bio: 1947 年生，美国认知神经科学家与发展心理学家，长期研究阅读的脑机制与诵读困难(dyslexia)。曾创办并主持塔夫茨大学(Tufts)阅读与语言研究中心，后转赴加州大学洛杉矶分校(UCLA)主持相关识字与诵读困难研究中心。代表作《普鲁斯特与乌贼：阅读如何改变我们的大脑》与《回家吧，阅读：数字时代我们该如何读书》。
wolf.bio_en: Born 1947, an American cognitive neuroscientist and developmental psychologist who has long studied the brain mechanisms of reading and dyslexia. She founded and directed the Center for Reading and Language Research at Tufts University, and later led a center for literacy and dyslexia research at UCLA. Her best-known books are 'Proust and the Squid: The Story and Science of the Reading Brain' and 'Reader, Come Home: The Reading Brain in a Digital World.'
wolf.ideas: 核心观点是：人脑并无与生俱来的『阅读回路』，阅读是相对晚近的文化发明，大脑要靠神经可塑性临时征用并连接原本用于视觉、语言与认知的区域才学会阅读。她提出『深度阅读』——推理、批判、共情、内省等需要时间的高阶加工；并警示数字时代的浅层略读可能弱化这条回路，主张培养能在纸质深读与数字速览间切换的『双语脑』，尤其关注儿童阅读脑的发育与早期识字。
wolf.ideas_en: Her central claim: the human brain has no innate 'reading circuit.' Reading is a relatively recent cultural invention, and the brain learns it only by using neuroplasticity to repurpose and wire together regions originally meant for vision, language, and cognition. She articulated 'deep reading'—the time-consuming higher-order processes of inference, critique, empathy, and reflection—and warned that the shallow skimming of the digital age may weaken that circuit. She argues for cultivating a 'biliterate brain' that can switch between deep print reading and fast digital skimming, with particular concern for the development of the reading brain in children and early literacy.

assessments.text: 被视为把阅读神经科学普及给大众的重要桥梁；其『阅读脑』框架(整合视觉、语言与认知的回路)被广泛引用于识字教育与诵读困难干预。
《回家吧，阅读》被广泛讨论为数字时代『深度阅读 vs 浅层略读』议题的代表性著作，影响了关于屏幕、儿童读写与注意力的公共讨论。

assessments_en.text: She is seen as a key bridge bringing the neuroscience of reading to a general audience; her 'reading brain' framework—a circuit integrating vision, language, and cognition—is widely cited in literacy education and dyslexia intervention.

'Reader, Come Home' is widely discussed as a defining book on the digital-age question of 'deep reading versus shallow skimming,' shaping public debate about screens, children's literacy, and attention.

quotes: 我们并非天生就会阅读……阅读是大脑的一项发明，每一代、每个孩子都要重新习得。(《普鲁斯特与乌贼》主旨，大意)
我们读什么、怎么读，正在塑造我们成为什么样的读者，乃至什么样的人。(其著作主旨，大意)
quotes_en: We were never born to read… reading is an invention of the brain that each generation, and each child, must acquire anew. (the thesis of 'Proust and the Squid,' paraphrased)
What we read, and how we read, is shaping the kind of readers—and the kind of people—we become. (the through-line of her work, paraphrased)

wolf.lineage: 承认知神经科学与发展心理学传统，并与诵读困难研究、识字教育实践紧密结合；其工作影响了数字时代关于屏幕、儿童读写与『深度阅读』的跨学科讨论。
wolf.lineage_en: She works in the tradition of cognitive neuroscience and developmental psychology, closely tied to dyslexia research and literacy education in practice; her work has shaped cross-disciplinary debate about screens, children's literacy, and 'deep reading' in the digital age.
wolf.trivia: 她曾坦言，在长期重度使用数字阅读后，重读年轻时挚爱的黑塞《玻璃球游戏》竟一度难以进入、读不下去——正是这段亲身经历促使她写作《回家吧，阅读》，并刻意重新训练自己的深度阅读能力。
wolf.trivia_en: She has candidly recounted that after years of heavy digital reading she found herself, for a time, unable to sink into Hermann Hesse's 'The Glass Bead Game,' a novel she had loved in her youth—an experience that prompted her to write 'Reader, Come Home' and to deliberately retrain her own capacity for deep reading.
